emails.subject: $10 vs. $10 million
emails.text:
BREAKING: Outside spending for Scott Wiener nears $10 MILLION

barallies,

I’m reaching out to ask you to chip in $10 to my campaign today. I hope you’ll let me explain why this request matters so much right now.

* My team just finished adding up the outside spending in this race: Super PACs and outside committees backing Scott Wiener have now spent nearly $10 MILLION to boost him and attack me.

* More than a third of that money has gone straight into attacks on me, landing just as voters are making up their minds.

* With five days until Election Day, we’re being outspent five to one.

If that’s all you need to hear, will you rush in $10 right now to help us answer nearly $10 million in outside spending?

Donate $10 >>

That money is landing right now, in the final days, when voters are making up their minds. The latest USC poll calls this race an effective tie, which means every voter we reach now could decide it.

I’ve never taken a dime of corporate PAC money, and I never will. This campaign runs on everyday San Franciscans. This weekend, our volunteers are knocking doors and making calls in Spanish, Chinese and English to reach every voter we can before Tuesday.

barallies, will you make a $10 donation to keep our volunteers on the doors through Election Day? Every $10 we raise is our answer to their $10 million.

Donate $10 >>

In solidarity,

Connie

emails.subject: Five days left, barallies
emails.text:
barallies,

Is there anything we can say to convince you to chip in $3 right now?

What if we told you that a USC poll found our race against Scott Wiener is essentially tied, with Election Day just five days away?

What if we told you that Super PACs and outside groups have already spent close to $8 million in this race, including nearly $3 million on attacks against Connie?

And what if we told you that Connie doesn’t take a dime of corporate PAC money, so the only thing standing between those Super PACs and this seat is grassroots supporters like you?

With five days until November 3rd, your $3 donation right now puts more volunteers at doors and on the phones with undecided voters. In a race this close, those conversations are what decide who wins.

Donate >>

Thank you,

Team Connie

emails.subject: Six days left. Here’s the list.
emails.text:
barallies,

Every day between now and Election Day, more ballots are returned across San Francisco. That leaves us six days to reach the voters who are still deciding, and here are six things they need to hear about how Scott Wiener has run this race:

* He built an AI chatbot that impersonated Connie. It mocked her accent as “so thick I can barely understand myself” and claimed her citizenship status was “classified.” His campaign advertised it on billboards across the city. And the site only came down after pressure from Nancy Pelosi and women leaders.

* He turned on leaders in his own party. Scott’s campaign has gone after Ro Khanna, who stood with Connie, and in Rep. Khanna’s words, Scott has been “echoing false right-wing attacks on Speaker Pelosi for over a year.”

* He denied the AI money on a debate stage. Hours before the debate, reporters revealed an Anthropic-funded group had put another $3 million into the Super PAC backing him, bringing its total to $3.5 million. Scott still lied to a theater full of San Franciscans, “There is no Anthropic money in this race.”

* His campaign is openly coordinating with a Super PAC. The Washington Sun reported that one of the Super PACs backing Scott works hand in hand with his campaign. It even paid the DJ at his birthday party and reported it as a “canvassing” expense.

* His own donor list tells you who he’d answer to. His campaign has taken money from real estate and pharmacy industry PACs.

* Now, we’re coming up short of our final October fundraising goal. Connie has never taken a dollar of corporate PAC money. Every organizer knocking doors between now and Election Day is paid for by grassroots supporters like you.

With six days until Election Day on November 3rd, a donation of $3 helps our organizers reach voters who haven’t returned their ballots yet. Can you donate now?

Donate >>

Thank you,

Team Connie

emails.subject: NEW POLL: 9% of voters will decide this
emails.text:
barallies,

A new USC poll of likely voters just came out, and the pollster behind it is calling our race against Scott Wiener “an effective tie.”

Christian Grose, who directs the USC lab, told SFGATE this is “really anyone’s race.”

The number we’re focused on is the 9% of likely voters who told pollsters they’re still undecided. That’s nearly one in ten voters who haven’t made up their minds. With one week until Election Day, they’re the people who will choose San Francisco’s next member of Congress.

Scott Wiener has a $3 million fundraising advantage, according to federal filings, and that’s before outside spending. Super PACs have already spent nearly $3 million attacking Connie, and outside groups have spent nearly $5 million more boosting him. They’re counting on mailers and ads to reach those undecided voters first.

Connie doesn’t take a dime of corporate PAC money. Her campaign runs on volunteers knocking doors, making calls, and talking to their neighbors.

With one week until Election Day, can you rush in $3 to help us reach the undecided voters who will decide this race? Every dollar powers the canvassing and phone banking that puts Connie’s message in front of them before November 3rd.

Donate >>

The pollster says this race is anyone’s to win. Let’s go win it.

Thank you,

Team Connie

emails.subject: Even $1 makes a difference
emails.text:
barallies, I'm coming to you with a simple – but meaningful – ask: I'm asking you to chip in just $1 today.

Donate $1 >>

I realize it may not seem like a lot, especially compared to what special interests are spending to try to buy this seat.

But if everyone reading this message gave $1, it would show a grassroots surge of support behind this movement. It would prove to Scott Wiener and everyone watching this race that the power of working people can defeat outside spending.

Every dollar you give moves us closer to coming out on top November 3rd – $1 helps us knock on one more door, print one more flyer, and reach one more voter in this critical final stretch.

That’s how grassroots campaigns win.

Not with billionaires.

Not with corporate PACs.

But with thousands of people stepping up together.

So today, I’m personally asking: Will you chip in just $1 – or any amount you can – to help us finish strong before the November 3rd general election?

Donate >>

In solidarity,

Connie

emails.subject: barallies, you’re not an ATM to me
emails.text:
With only 9 days until Election Day, barallies, your inbox is probably full of ALL CAPS subject lines and “matches” that triple every dollar. Mine is too.

I’m not going to write to you that way. You’re not an ATM, and I don’t expect you to give every time you hear from me.

But I don’t take corporate PAC money. So when the super PACs backing Scott Wiener buy another round of ads, people like you are the ones who make our response possible.

There’s no fake deadline here. Election Day is November 3rd, and that one’s real. If you’re able, can you rush in $3 to keep our volunteers talking with voters through these final nine days? It all goes toward reaching voters before they mail their ballots.

Donate >>

If now isn’t the right time, I understand. Thank you for reading.

In solidarity,

emails.subject: 11 days. $11. CA-11.
emails.text:
Hi barallies,

At the end of this email, I’m going to ask you to donate $11 to my campaign in California’s 11th Congressional District. Here’s why your support matters right now.

Donate $11 >>

Election Day is 11 days away , and voters across CA-11 are locking in their choice.

I came to San Francisco from Hong Kong as a first-generation immigrant. I’ve spent two decades fighting for working families in this city, because I know what it’s like to be the family that gets overlooked.

And it’s why watching who’s lining up behind Scott Wiener is so frustrating.

Corporate-backed super PACs are spending heavily on TV ads and mailers to help him win. They’re counting on voters hearing from them before they ever hear from us.

This race will come down to who reaches voters in these final days. We can win it, but only if we keep our momentum going now.

Every attack against me needs an answer before voters lock in their choice. With 11 days left, will you donate $11 for CA-11 so we can respond to Scott Wiener’s attacks?

Donate $11 >>

In solidarity,

Connie

emails.subject: re: your mailbox
emails.text:
barallies,

Getting a lot of these?
Mailers

Before you believe the lies filling up your mailbox, look at who’s paying for them. Super PACs are spending big to elect Scott Wiener, including an AI group funded by Anthropic that has put in $3.5 million. They’d like you to focus on the attack mailers instead of the corporate money behind his campaign.

That money has a purpose. AI runs on data centers, and companies are racing to build them in communities across the country – including San Francisco. They use enormous amounts of electricity and water, and working families end up paying for it on their utility bills. I support a nationwide moratorium on new data centers until Congress puts real protections in place.

I’m the only candidate in this race who does.

I don’t take corporate PAC money. I will hold AI companies accountable, protect our jobs, and make billionaires pay their fair share. Big Tech can buy a mailbox full of attacks, but they cannot buy my vote in Congress.

So barallies, if you’re sick and tired of these mailers, then you should vote, and vote early. Once you vote, they will remove you from their mail list, so you can put an end to that junk mail.

With less than two weeks until November 3rd, the mailers aren’t slowing down, and neither can we. Can you chip in $3 to put our message in front of voters before they fill out their ballots?

Donate >>

In solidarity,

Connie

emails.subject: doors or phones?
emails.text:
barallies,

With two weeks left, this race comes down to one question: can a campaign built by working people beat one backed by billionaire and corporate money?

Corporate money doesn’t show up in our elections by accident. Billionaires and big corporations, including the AI industry, spend in our elections because the people they help elect end up writing the rules in their favor. Most families in this city will never write those kinds of checks, and Congress should still work for them.

I came to San Francisco from Hong Kong as a 13-year-old immigrant. I’ve spent two decades fighting for working families here, most recently as Budget Chair on the Board of Supervisors. I know who gets heard in government when nobody pushes back.

That’s why I run this campaign differently. I’ve never taken a dollar of corporate PAC money. Our campaign is funded by people giving what they can, when they can, and our voter conversations happen because volunteers chose to give up an evening or a Saturday, at the door or on the phone.

Ballots are already in voters’ hands, and plenty of them haven’t been filled out yet. Every one of those voters needs a real conversation before they decide, and in these last two weeks, there are two ways to make that happen: your time and your money.

Will you sign up for a volunteer shift before November 3rd? You can knock doors with us in San Francisco or join a phone bank from wherever you are, and our organizers will get you set up to talk with voters who haven’t returned their ballots yet.

PICK A SHIFT: DOORS OR PHONES

The other way to help is with a donation. It pays for the organizers and walk lists behind every one of those conversations.

When the results come in, I want them to show that a campaign built by thousands of ordinary people giving what they can can win in this city. Can you chip in $5 to help get us there?

Donate >>

In solidarity,

Connie

emails.subject: Who’s writing Scott’s checks?
emails.text:
barallies,

For the first time in decades, San Francisco is choosing a new representative in Congress.

The person who wins will make decisions in Washington that shape whether working families can still afford to build a life here. How each candidate runs this race tells you a lot about who they’ll answer to once they get there.

Scott Wiener keeps showing us his answer.

The Washington Sun reported that Scott’s campaign and one of the super PACs backing him are openly coordinating, and the super PAC even paid the DJ at Scott’s birthday party as a “canvassing” expense. That super PAC can take checks too big for Scott’s own campaign to legally accept.

The Washington Sun
Pelosi's Potential Successor is Pushing the Limits of Super PAC Coordination
Spending records raise questions about Democrat Scott Wiener's open coordination with Families for an Affordable San Francisco

That’s the outside money. Scott’s own campaign takes industry money too. His latest FEC report shows he received money from a senior Palantir executive involved in its ICE work, Flock Safety’s public affairs leader, and other special interests.

Between his super PAC and his own donor list, it’s getting easy to see who Scott would answer to in Congress.

Connie is offering a different choice. She came to San Francisco from Hong Kong as a 13-year-old immigrant and has spent two decades fighting for working families. She doesn’t accept corporate PAC money, so the people she answers to are the San Franciscans who send her to Congress.

With two weeks until Election Day on November 3rd, a donation of $3 helps Connie reach voters before they mark their ballots. Your support puts this choice in front of San Franciscans while there’s still time to make it.

Donate >>

Thank you,

Team Connie

emails.subject: I’m a proud Labor Democrat. Here’s what that means:
emails.text:
I want to speak to you directly about what I’m really up against in this race.

I’m a proud Labor Democrat. I believe in the labor movement, and I know working people need a fighting champion in Congress. That’s why the California Labor Federation put its full weight behind this campaign.

We’re facing off against corporate Democrats.

They say all the right things. Then a bill for Medicare for All comes up, or the funding our public schools need, or making billionaires and big corporations pay their fair share, and they never cast that vote.

They’ve had decades in Sacramento and Washington. Look at what happened to the rest of us: rent has never been higher, utility bills have never been higher, and families are still falling through the gaps in our health care and our schools.

The super PACs backing Scott Wiener are now on track to spend millions against me. You can decide for yourself why they’d pay that much to keep a Labor Democrat out of Congress.

I’ve never taken a dollar of corporate PAC money. On day one, I’ll co-sponsor Medicare for All, and the only people I’ll answer to are the ones who sent me there.

Ballots are in mailboxes, and voters are deciding right now what kind of Democrat represents this city. Will you chip in $3 to help elect a Labor Democrat who will actually cast the vote?

Donate >>

In solidarity,

Connie

So many voters tell our volunteers, “I haven’t decided yet.” I love that answer, because it means a real person is ready to ask a real question and hear an honest answer.

You can help make sure we have as many of those conversations as possible. Will you chip in $5 to our Field Fund today? It goes directly to the volunteers and organizers talking with undecided voters.

If this is your first contribution, $5 still counts toward our field goal and helps keep our volunteers knocking doors through November 3rd.Donate >>

emails.subject: “There is no Anthropic money in this race.”
emails.text:
Let me recap Tuesday’s debate, barallies.

Just hours before Scott Wiener and I took the stage, reporters revealed that Public First Action, an AI group funded by Anthropic, had poured another $3 million into a super PAC backing Scott. That brings the group’s total to $3,500,000 to put him in Congress.

The moderators asked him about it. Twice.

Scott looked out at a theater full of San Franciscans and said, “There is no Anthropic money in this race.” Then he kept saying it.

Here’s what he left out: Anthropic has given Public First Action $40 million. That’s half of everything it has raised.

Scott would rather repeat the same lie over and over than explain where $3.5 million came from. I’ll let you decide what it says about him.

I asked him directly on that stage: How can San Franciscans, and people across this country, trust you to regulate AI with integrity, and not just placate the industry?

He dodged the question.

Scott wants to be the person writing the federal rules for AI. The industry clearly wants that too. I don’t take a dime of corporate PAC money, so nobody is paying for my answers on this.

Ballots are already in voters’ hands, and Election Day is November 3rd. We can’t match Scott’s AI money dollar for dollar, but we can make sure voters hear the truth from us.

Will you chip in $3 so voters hear what Scott wouldn’t say on that debate stage? If $3 is too much right now, any amount helps keep our organizers talking with voters through November 3rd.

Donate >>

In solidarity,

Connie

emails.subject: Over $1 million spent attacking Connie
emails.text:
We wanted you to have these numbers, barallies:

Super PACs have now spent over $1 million attacking Connie in this race.

That figure only counts money spent against her. The separate spending to boost Scott Wiener comes on top of it.

Here’s what was just added:

* Abundant Future , the Super PAC that took $500,000 from Anthropic, reported $146,250 for streaming ads against Connie. Those ads will be playing on voters’ screens while their ballots sit on the kitchen table.

* GrowUSA , the GrowSF offshoot backed by crypto and Big Tech money, reported paying a political consultant to work against Connie and for Scott, plus another round of digital ads.

Connie doesn’t take corporate PAC money. Our answer is people. Ballots went out Monday, and our organizers are talking with voters every day between now and November 3rd. And Connie’s own ad is on the air, paid for one grassroots donation at a time.

The billionaires and Big AI have spent over a million dollars to get between Connie and the voters of this city. But they can’t buy the volunteers who knock on a neighbor’s door because they believe in this movement.

Every attack ad that runs this month needs an answer from someone voters trust. A donation of $3 from you would go a long way to keep our organizers talking with voters through Election Day.

Donate >>

Thank you,

Team Connie

emails.subject: Ballots are in mailboxes now 🗳️

barallies,

Now my name is printed on the ballot sitting in mailboxes across San Francisco.

Between now and November 3rd, voters get to decide what kind of leader should represent them in Congress, and I trust them to answer that. But when they see my name on that ballot, I want them to know exactly what it stands for. I said it as plainly as I could when I closed last Thursday's debate:

"It is time to make sure that working people have a win. We deserve a win."

Donate >>

That's the message I want in front of every voter while they're deciding. A lot of voters fill out their ballots within days of opening them, so this week is our best chance to reach them first. Our volunteers will be out across the city while ballots are still on kitchen counters, waiting to be filled out, and what we raise now decides how many of those conversations we can have.

I don't take corporate PAC money, so those conversations only happen because people like you fund them.

Will you chip in $3 to help our team reach as many voters as possible while their ballots are fresh in hand? Every voter we reach now hears from us while their ballot is still blank.

In solidarity,

Connie

emails.subject: Your ballot checklist, barallies 🗳️
emails.text:
barallies,

Tomorrow, Monday, October 5, ballots start going out to voters across San Francisco. Before yours arrives, our team put together a quick checklist to help you get ready for the four weeks that decide this race.

1. Make sure your ballot finds you 🗳️
Sign up at https://california.ballottrax.net/voter/ to get a text or email when your ballot is mailed, received, and counted. If you've moved recently, you can update your registration through October 19th.

2. Follow Connie online 📲
Connie will be posting from the campaign trail all month, from neighborhood canvasses to community events. Follow her on Instagram and Facebook . Sharing even one of her posts puts her name in front of a friend who hasn't heard it yet.

3. Join us on the doors (or the phones) 🚪
Our volunteers will be out across the city as ballots land, talking with neighbors in the Richmond, the Excelsior, and everywhere in between. Weekend canvasses work great if you're local. If you're not, you can make calls from your couch. Sign up for a shift here .

4. Show your support 🪧
A window sign or a Connie shirt does more than you'd think, especially when your neighbors are sitting down with their ballots. Grab yours here.

5. Chip in if you're able 💛
Connie has never taken a dime of corporate PAC money, so this campaign runs on grassroots supporters. After a busy end of quarter, we'll keep the ask simple: if you're in a position to give $3, it helps keep our organizers talking with voters through the weeks when they're actually filling out their ballots.

Donate >>

Thank you for being part of this,

Team Connie

P.S. Know someone in San Francisco who'd want this checklist? Forward it their way before their ballot shows up.

emails.subject: One month from today
emails.text:
Election day is one month from today, barallies.

I want to tell you how I'm thinking about these final 31 days, because it's the same way I've approached every budget I've written as Chair of San Francisco's Budget Committee.

A budget shows what you actually value. Anyone can say they care about seniors, tenants, and working families, but the numbers reveal whether they mean it.

Our campaign's budget for this last month works the same way. Starting Monday, as ballots begin reaching voters, what we raise goes toward talking with them directly. That might be an organizer at a door in the Richmond, or a mailer that lands in Visitacion Valley the same week a ballot does.

There's one line you won't find anywhere in our budget, and that's corporate PAC money. I've never taken a dime of it, even as corporate-backed super PACs line up behind Scott Wiener.

If you're able to chip in $3, it will go straight into reaching San Francisco voters during the month that decides this race. And if you gave before Wednesday's deadline, thank you, because you're a big part of why this budget exists at all.

Donate >>

In solidarity,

emails.subject: Did you catch the debate?
emails.text:
barallies, did you catch the debate?

I stood across from Scott Wiener and asked a question that every San Francisco voter deserves an answer to: can we trust politicians who are bankrolled by the AI industry to regulate it?

The answer is no. We cannot.

Scott has built his campaign on AI industry money. An Anthropic-backed super PAC committed $500,000 to help him defeat me. Last night, he tried to have it both ways: claiming to fight Big Tech corporations while cashing their checks.

I said it plainly on that stage: workers and unions need to be at the table to regulate this technology. Not the billionaires funding his campaign. Not the super PACs spending half a million to put him in Congress.

The same industry he claims he wants to regulate is now commissioning polls and spending half a million dollars to push him over the finish line. You have to ask yourself why.

You’ll never hear a mixed message on this from me. America can be a leader in innovation without sacrificing safety and our workforce. That's what I believe. That's what I'll fight for in Congress.

With 32 days left, Big AI is spending big to drown us out. The only thing that stops them is a grassroots movement that refuses to quit. Will you chip in $3 to help us fight back against the AI lobby’s meddling in this race?

Thank you,Connie

emails.subject: Labor Day message from Connie's campaign manager
emails.sender: Rudy Gonzalez, via Connie Chan for Congress
emails.text:
barallies,

This is Rudy Gonzalez. I've spent my career in the labor movement — first as a Teamster at 18, then leading the San Francisco Labor Council, and now as secretary-treasurer of the SF Building & Construction Trades Council.

I didn't expect to take a leave of absence from my work at the Building Trades to run a congressional campaign. But when Connie asked, I didn't hesitate.

I want to tell you why.

I've watched Connie show up for working people in this city for years. Not just at endorsement time — at the picket line. At the budget table, fighting to protect union jobs when City Hall wanted to cut them. In the halls of power, standing up for the nurses, teachers, firefighters, hotel workers, and building trades members who actually make San Francisco run.

She's been there, again and again, when it counted.

This Labor Day, I want to say something that gets lost in the noise of a big congressional race: the most powerful thing we have isn't a TV ad or a super PAC. It's people. Organized people, showing up together, having real conversations with their neighbors. That's how labor wins. And that's how this campaign is going to win. Scott Wiener has the billionaires. He has the crypto donors and the corporate PACs. We have something better — a movement of working people who believe San Francisco shouldn't be for sale.

But movements need people to show up. This Labor Day weekend, I'm asking you to join us — knock a door, make some calls, show a neighbor why this race matters. If you can't make it out, a contribution to keep our organizers on the ground can go just as far.

This is how we win. Not by outspending them — by outworking them.

In solidarity,

Rudy Gonzalez
Campaign Manager

Thank you,

Connie

emails.subject: Still just $1
emails.text:
$1.

That's what we're asking you to chip in to Connie's campaign today.

Donate $1

Defeating Scott Wiener was never going to be about matching his money. It's about out-organizing him – door-by-door, conversation-by-conversation, across every neighborhood in San Francisco.

That kind of organizing isn't free. Every $1 adds up to real things:

$1 helps keep our volunteers knocking doors across the Sunset, the Mission, Bayview and every corner of this district.

$1 helps us reach voters by text and phone who we'd never find otherwise – and in multiple languages.

$1 proves, one more time, that this campaign is powered by people – not billionaire Super PAC checks.

Scott Wiener has Big Tech, crypto donors, and corporate PACs supporting him. What we have is people like you, showing up again and again, in amounts as small as $1.

With our end-of-month deadline closing in tomorrow, can you chip in $1 to help us keep showing up all the way to November?

Thank you,

Team Connie

emails.subject: My opponent’s “MAGA fan club”
emails.text:
barallies,

Scott Wiener likes to brag about his "MAGA fan club" of right-wing critics.

But let's talk about his actual fan club.

There are two super PACs spending big right now to put him in Congress. One is funded by Big Tech and crypto special interests. Another – GrowUSA – is bankrolled by a network of billionaire corporate donors.

When you look at who's behind this network, some of the same executives writing big checks to boost Scott have written big checks to boost Donald Trump.

That's Scott's real MAGA fan club.

While billionaire donors spend whatever it takes to buy this seat, we're building a movement powered by nurses, teachers, firefighters, union members, tenants, and working families who actually make San Francisco run.

My opponent can have the Trump donors and billionaires.

I'll take the people.

Our end-of-month deadline hits in two days and we still need some help hitting our goal. Will you chip in $3 to prove that people-power beats big money?

In solidarity,

Connie

emails.subject: Here's the latest in the race for CA-11.
emails.text:
barallies,

In a moment, we're going to ask you to make a grassroots donation of $3 to our campaign. But before we do, here's what you need to know right now:

The latest poll has us within striking distance. It's 45-40 in Scott Wiener's favor, but we've seen an upward swing of 10-points since the primary. Connie has the momentum.

A new super PAC funded by billionaire tech executives and Trump donors announced $400,000 in new ads to boost Wiener's campaign. That should tell you everything you need to know about the interests propping him up.

We set a goal of raising $25,000 in online donations before the end of this week to keep pace. As it stands, we're coming up a bit short.

If you've been watching this race and waiting for when your dollars would make a huge impact — this is it. Please chip in $3 today to help us close the gap on our goal.

Thank you,

Team Connie

emails.subject: I'm not who they expected
emails.text:
barallies,

We're just days away from our end-of-month deadline, and we need your support. You can chip in $3 before it hits, and let me explain.

People have asked me this: Can you really handle Congress?

I'm an immigrant. I speak with an accent. I'm a working mom.

And for a long time, that was enough for some people to question whether I belonged in rooms where decisions were made. Now as we face the halls of Congress it continues to be a question. But when they see a white man in a suit, there's no question.

But for women, and women of color? The standard is different.

We have to prove ourselves over and over again.
We have to be better than great.
We have to be perfect.

That standard is almost impossible. So I'm flipping this question on its head: Can Congress handle me?

I'm not going to Washington to fit in. I'm going to fight for working families, I'm going to stand up to big money, and I'm going to bring the voices of San Francisco to the forefront – whether the status quo is ready for it or not.

So right now, we need your help to prove that this campaign can go toe-to-toe against these standards AND WIN. If you're with me, if you chip in $3 before our end-of-month deadline, your contribution will help send a message that we aren't backing down.

In solidarity,

Connie

emails.subject: Scott Wiener hurls attacks at Speaker Pelosi and Ro Khanna.
emails.text:
Scott Wiener seems to have forgotten he's running against Connie. He's now going after all the people who stand with her.

Politico reported this morning that his flailing campaign has been attacking both Nancy Pelosi and Ro Khanna – two respected leaders in our party – ever since Ro stood alongside Connie at a union hall here in San Francisco.

This isn't new for Scott. As Rep. Khanna put it, Wiener has been "echoing false right-wing attacks on Speaker Pelosi for over a year."

He'll do or say anything to win. And it's starting to show.

Meanwhile, Connie is doing what she's always done: knocking doors, building a coalition of labor, educators, and working families, and staying focused on the fight that actually matters.

Lashing out isn't a winning – or a governing – strategy. This is what desperation looks like.

With our end-of-month deadline hitting August 31st, every dollar is a vote for the kind of politics Connie represents. Will you chip in $3 before midnight on the 31st to help fuel this movement all the way to November?

Thank you,

Team Connie

emails.subject: The only model of politics I trust
emails.text:
Six days left in August, barallies.

Every month, my fundraising team sets a goal -- it's what tells us whether we can keep paying the people knocking doors across this district, keep the phones running, and keep our campaign visible in every neighborhood. That number is the difference between a field program that runs strong into November and one that has to pull back.

For this month, we're not quite to our goal yet.

I grew up in a family that had no political power and no connections. Nobody handed us anything. What we had was each other -- and the people who showed up when it counted. That's the only model of politics I trust, and the only way I know how to run a campaign.

This final week isn't about panic. It's about continuing what we said we'd do. A campaign like this doesn't run on a handful of big checks -- it runs on hundreds of people deciding, month after month, that this is worth a few dollars. That's what gets us to the number we need by the 31st.

Can you help us get there? $3 or whatever you're able to give is exactly what we need to get across the finish line.

In solidarity,

Connie

emails.subject: Town Hall Recap
emails.text:
Dear barallies,

Last week, we held a town hall with Congressman Ro Khanna and the California Working Families Party to discuss some of the most important issues for voters.

How do we fight back against Trump? How do we prevent families from being priced out of the Bay Area? How do we fund priorities nationwide like Medicare for All, universal childcare, and Free City College?

The answer is pretty simple: We put working families before corporations. We make sure billionaires pay their fair share. We stop spending $1.5 trillion on war, and invest that money back into our communities.

I am grateful that Congressman Ro Khanna and California Working Families Party Director Jorge Contreras joined us at our town hall to talk with voters on how to stand up for working Californians in Washington D.C.

Our worker-centric policies are why corporate interests are spending big to prevent us from winning this seat. But I know we've got the people-power to beat them.

Can you join us for a volunteer shift this week to help spread the word about Connie?

Join us for a volunteer shift this week!

Saturday, August 29th we will be canvassing in Glen Park at 10am. We will meet at the entrance of Glen Canyon Park on Chenery & Elk Streets. RSVP here.

Sunday we will be canvassing in the Mission. Meet at our campaign headquarters at 3043 24th Street. RSVP here to join.

Every Tuesday and Thursday join us as we phonebank voters from our Campaign HQ.

Interested in visibility? Swing by the office (3043 24th St, San Francisco, CA 94110) anytime between 10am-6pm on weekdays and we'll get you set up to do visibility at a farmers market, or put up signs in your local neighborhood corridor.

Thanks for all your support.

In solidarity,
Team Connie

emails.subject: I want to show you something in his own campaign's filings:
emails.text:
barallies, this is a long, but important email about the troubling stories emerging about my opponent's campaign finances. I hope you'll take a moment to read this whole message, then chip in $3 to help us keep running our campaign the right way.

For decades, strict firewall rules kept congressional campaigns from coordinating directly with super PACs. That wall existed for a reason: super PACs can raise unlimited corporate cash, and keeping them separate was the last line of defense against billionaires and special interests outright bankrolling a candidate's campaign.

In 2024, the FEC created a loophole. And Scott Wiener's campaign didn't just take full advantage — they went even further.

FEC filings show the super PAC behind Scott has been paying the same staffers to work in the same office at the same time under the same leadership as Wiener's congressional campaign.

I'll let you decide what it says about a candidate when the very first thing he does with a weaker rule is test its limits.

This is the difference between us. I don't take corporate PAC money. I never have. Every dollar in this campaign is one I can look you in the eye about — raised from people who believe in our mission, not special interests who expect something in return.

Money can buy ads. It can buy staff time twice over if you're clever about which entity cuts the check. What it can't buy is the trust we've built door-to-door, house by house, across this district.

Will you chip in $3 to help us keep building this campaign the honest way?

In solidarity,

Connie

emails.subject: before you scroll past this
emails.text:
We wanted to make sure you saw Connie's note, barallies.

She's spent two decades fighting for working families in San Francisco. Her opponent, Scott Wiener, took Big Tech money and let an AI chatbot mock her accent, her background, even her citizenship – then plastered it on billboards across the city.

When Nancy Pelosi and leaders across the state called him out, Scott attacked them. Then he shrugged the whole thing off as a "political experiment" that just "missed the mark."

That's not an apology. That's not leadership.

This race is neck and neck and will come down to grassroots support from folks like you in 94114. Will you chip in $3 right now?

Donate $3

Thank you,

Team Connie

---------- Forwarded message ----------

barallies,

I want to tell you something Scott Wiener's AI chatbot said about me.

It mocked my accent as "so thick I can barely understand myself." It made jokes about my birth certificate being "tied up in committee." It claimed my citizenship status is "classified." And it was plastered on billboards across San Francisco.

I came to this city as a first-generation American immigrant from Hong Kong. I built my life here. I raised my family here. And I have spent two decades fighting for the working families of San Francisco.

That is what drives me and who I fight for every day. That is who Scott Wiener chose to mock.

Under pressure from Nancy Pelosi and leaders across our city and state, he eventually took it down. But he never took real responsibility – he first doubled down by blaming our campaign and said the political experiment just "missed the mark."

I'll let you decide what that says about his character and judgement.

Recent polling has this race neck and neck, and we have a clear path to victory in November. Scott Wiener has the AI industry's money behind him. We have you – will you chip in $3 right now to power our campaign for Congress?

In solidarity,

Connie
(The real me)

emails.subject: Another super PAC is jumping in for Scott Wiener.
emails.text:
barallies,

The corporate cavalry just arrived for Scott Wiener.

A brand-new super PAC called GrowUSA launched with one purpose: a billionaire bailout for Scott's campaign. They're starting with $400,000 — and they've made clear they'll spend significantly more before November.

This is what it looks like when Big Tech and corporate money decide they want to buy an election because their candidate is in trouble. GrowUSA is an offshoot of GrowSF, the same crypto, tech, and venture capital backed outfit that has tried to sway San Francisco politics for years.

We can't match a super PAC dollar for dollar. But we've never had to — because we've built this campaign door by door, neighborhood by neighborhood, in every language spoken in this city. That's what they can't buy.

$400,000 is just the opening bid, and every day we don't respond is another day that money hits airwaves and mailboxes unchallenged. Will you chip in $3 right now to make sure their money doesn't drown out our movement?

In solidarity,

Team Connie

emails.subject: The stakes just changed.
emails.sender: Adam Schiff, via Connie Chan for Congress
emails.text:
barallies,

Donald Trump fired every remaining commissioner of the federal agency that helps states run secure elections.

By email. Effective immediately. Just months before the midterms.

Days earlier, his Justice Department announced it was deploying election monitors to battleground states and Democratic strongholds — and threatened election officials in all 50 states with criminal prosecution.

Fired the referees. Sent in his own watchers. Threatened the people who count the votes.

I spent years as a federal prosecutor. I know a pattern of intent when I see one. This isn't election security — it's an attempt to seize control of our elections before a single ballot is cast.

There is one check on his abuse of power that Trump cannot fire and cannot intimidate: a Democratic Congress.

That's why we're scaling up our operations right now — expanding the infrastructure it will take to hold him accountable and retake the Congress.

barallies, will you split a contribution between Connie Chan and me to help us defend our elections and win back Congress?

Trump is betting that Americans won't notice. That we won't fight back.

He's wrong on both counts. I've stood up to him before — through impeachment, through censure, through my service on the January 6th Committee, through every smear he's thrown at me — and I'm not about to stop now.

Thank you for your support.

— Adam
